scenes.headline: How a plain-language spec compiles into tiny weights
scenes.sub: Program-as-Weights: a 4B compiler, a LoRA adapter, a frozen 0.6B interpreter.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Boson! Some functions are too fuzzy for rules. Program-as-Weights compiles them into tiny local models. Here's how.

scenes.text: Compile a fuzzy function once, from a plain-language spec into a small LoRA adapter. A frozen 0.6B model runs it locally.
scenes.say: The idea: compile a fuzzy function once, from plain words into a small adapter. Then a tiny frozen model runs it locally, forever.

scenes.title: From a spec to a running function

steps.say: Write the function in plain words, like repair malformed JSON. A four-billion-parameter compiler, trained on ten million fuzzy functions, reads it once.
It doesn't write raw weights. A small network mixes a set of learned low-rank basis matrices.
That mix is a LoRA adapter: a compact program you own.
Load it into a frozen interpreter of zero point six billion parameters, and it runs on every input, locally, at thirty tokens a second on a MacBook.

scenes.title: Pay per call, or pay once

left.title: Call a big API
left.say: The usual move is to ask a big model's API every time. You pay on every call, and give up locality and reproducibility.

right.title: Compile once, run locally
items: Then each call is nearly free
right.say: Here you pay for one compile, then every call runs locally for almost nothing. The big model builds the tool instead of doing the job.

scenes.label: the inference memory of prompting Qwen3-32B directly, at matching quality
scenes.say: The payoff: the small interpreter matches prompting Qwen3-32B directly, with about one-fiftieth of the memory. That parity is on the fuzzy tasks it was built for.

scenes.text: Treat a foundation model as a compiler for behaviors, not an always-on oracle.

scenes.say: To recap: compile the spec once, run the adapter locally, and stop paying per call.
